assign.outcome:
**Provenance is universal and read-only — and the first slice already ships.** Select anything on the site and the drawer now ends in a **css** group: one row per rule the browser is actually applying, each tagged with the **part** that owns it (framework / lew42 / site / the module dir). 24 new lines in `ext/CSSDoc/CSSDoc.js` (`cssdoc.rules()`, `cssdoc.part()`) and one 12-line `defined($el)` in `ext/layout/body.js`.

![](drawer.png)

**The finding that shapes the rest: the `@layer` is not the part.** `.sidebar` returns `Page theme`, `Sidebar theme` and `site site`; `.page-title` returns `framework theme` and `lew42 theme` — four owners, one layer name, because `framework.css` alone writes base, theme AND util. Only the sheet href says what else a change will affect.

**The two-up defect, confirmed live:** `ext/demo/layout.js:71-72` hands only `$views[0]` to `steer()` and `toggles()`, and `layout.bar()` is the ONLY caller of `region()` (`ext/layout/layout.js:37`) — so selectability is welded to the toolbar. Measured on `/framework/styles/layouts/docs/`: 2 panes, **1 `.layout-region`, on the wide left one**. Clicking the right pane selects nothing *and deselects*. Fix is S: export `layout.selectable()`, call it on both panes, register the context on `$stage`.
